soundcheck.heard: Alaska buried seismometers to hear earthquakes. Researchers taught 200 of those sensors a second job, hearing landslides. A quake ends in seconds. A slide rumbles for a minute. A program watches for that. It searches only one stretch of coast. Last August, a mountain fell into Tracy arm. South of Juneau. It fell outside the search area, so no alarm fired. The sensors still heard it. A scientist found the slide by hand. And a harder limit remains. Rock makes no sound until it falls. So a federal grant sent $1.77 million to the University of Alaska Fairbanks to build a simulated mountain fed by those sensors that forecasts what a slope will do. The work starts next month and takes years. The sensors keep listening. But never ahead.
